claims.explanation: SB-590885 is a selective BRAF inhibitor that kills cancer lines dependent on oncogenic BRAF signaling, so BRAF-mutant lines (especially V600E-like melanoma, colorectal, thyroid, and endometrial lines) are most sensitive. Conversely, lines driven by KRAS/NRAS or by RTK/RAS activation upstream of RAF, or with PI3K/PTEN pathway alterations that provide RAF-independent survival, are relatively resistant. The pattern is consistent with oncogenic BRAF mutation as the primary sensitizing feature and RAS/PI3K pathway activation as protective.

features.basis: Oncogenic BRAF is the validated target and predicts selective MAPK inhibition (PMID 17145850, 16260133)
RAS mutations activate RAF/MEK/ERK independently of BRAF inhibition and are enriched in resistant lines
KRAS-driven MAPK signaling bypasses BRAF dependence and is enriched in least-affected lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling, a known resistance mechanism to BRAF inhibitors (PMID 21156289)
PI3K pathway activation provides RAF-independent survival and is seen in several resistant lines
NF1 loss activates RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and may increase dependence on BRAF/MEK signaling
MEK1 mutation can activate ERK downstream of RAF and reduce dependence on BRAF (PMID 17981815)
EGFR-driven RTK signaling activates RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK upstream of BRAF and is seen in resistant lung lines
IGF-1R/PI3K signaling mediates acquired resistance to BRAF inhibitors (PMID 21156289)
Higher BRAF expression may increase dependence on the drug's target
Observed in several sensitive BRAF-mutant lines but mechanism unclear
TP53 mutation is common across both groups and not selective; included only as weak negative evidence
